Masayoshi Son’s $20 million bet on Alibaba became one of the greatest venture capital investments in history. 💰 In 2000, Son met a relatively unknown Jack Ma and reportedly spent only a few minutes with him before deciding to invest. Instead of relying entirely on financial projections, Son believed in Ma’s vision and the potential of his company. SoftBank eventually secured roughly a 30% stake in Alibaba. What started as a $20 million investment later became worth billions as Alibaba grew into one of the world’s biggest technology companies. Interestingly, Son initially wanted to invest $40 million, but Jack Ma reportedly accepted only $20 million because he believed that was enough to build the business. The lesson? Sometimes the biggest investments are made before the numbers look obvious. Would you invest based on a founder’s vision—or wait for the financial data to prove it? Ordering furniture from China isn’t as simple as finding a cute sofa on Alibaba and hitting “add to cart.” 😂 There’s a whole process between finding the furniture and having that container sitting at your warehouse. Manufacturers. Negotiations. Production. Freight. Customs. Port fees. Final delivery. And baby… there are PLENTY of opportunities to make an expensive mistake in between. Ask me how I know. 😭😂 I’ve been importing inventory for years, and learning how to source overseas completely changed the way I was able to grow my rental inventory. So if importing is something you’re seriously considering, learn the process BEFORE you start sending people your money. I put what I’ve learned—including manufacturers I’ve actually sourced from—inside my Luxury Inventory Sourcing Blueprint. Comment IMPORT and I’ll send you the information. 💕 Learn first. Then spend.
